chapterNote: Chapter 8 is Wisdom's great public sermon, the answer to the seductress of chapter 7. She does not whisper in shadowed doorways but cries aloud at the city gates, where every road meets and all of life is decided (vv. 1-11). She lays out her gifts — counsel, strength, the just rule of kings, riches that endure (vv. 12-21) — and then, in the chapter's soaring center, she traces her own origin: brought forth by the LORD before the world began, present as His master craftsman when He framed the heavens and bounded the sea, daily His delight and delighting in the sons of men (vv. 22-31). The chapter ends with life and death set before the hearer: whoever finds Wisdom finds life and the LORD's favor, but whoever spurns her loves death (vv. 32-36). The Christian church has long heard in this self-portrait a foreshadowing of Christ, the eternal Wisdom and Word by whom all things were made (John 1:1-3; 1 Cor 1:24, 30; Col 1:16).

1.text: Does not Wisdom call aloud? Does not Understanding lift up her voice?
1.amp: Does not Wisdom [chokmah — skill in living] cry out [qara — call, proclaim], and Understanding [tebunah — discernment, the trained mind] send forth her voice [qol]?
1.notes: chokmah (H2451) and tebunah (H8394) are personified as a woman preaching in public — the deliberate counter-image to the 'strange woman' of chapter 7. Her voice is open and free, the opposite of seduction's secrecy.

2.text: On the heights beside the road, at the crossroads where the paths meet, there she takes her stand.
2.amp: She stands [natsab — takes her stand, stations herself] at the top [rosh — head, summit] of the high places [marom — the heights], by the way [derek], where the paths [netivah] meet she is stationed.
2.notes: natsab (H5324) is to plant oneself firmly and on purpose. Wisdom posts herself at the most public, most-traveled ground — the summit, the highway, the crossroads — so that no one passing through life can claim he never heard her.

3.text: Beside the gates, at the mouth of the city, at the entryways she cries aloud:
3.amp: Beside the gates [shaar — the city gate], at the mouth [peh — mouth, opening] of the town, at the coming in of the doorways [petach — entrance, opening], she cries aloud [ranan — shouts, sings out].
3.notes: the city gate (shaar, H8179) was the ancient courtroom, marketplace, and town hall in one; ranan (H7442) is a full-throated, ringing cry. Wisdom preaches at the seat of public life, refusing to be a private matter or a quiet hobby.

4.text: To you, O men, I am calling, and my voice goes out to all the sons of mankind.
4.amp: To you, O men [ish — man, each individual], I call [qara]; my voice [qol] is to the sons [ben] of mankind [adam — humanity, the race of Adam].
4.notes: the appeal is universal: ish (H376) names men one by one, while bene adam (H1121 + H120) sweeps in the whole human family. Wisdom excludes no one — her summons reaches the great man and the common one alike.

5.text: You who are simple, learn to be shrewd; you who are fools, gain an understanding heart.
5.amp: You simple ones [peti — the naive, easily led], understand [biyn — discern] prudence [ormah — shrewdness, street-sense]; you fools [kesil — the dull, correction-proof], be of an understanding [biyn] heart [leb].
5.notes: peti (H6612) is the open, persuadable young man; kesil (H3684) the thick-headed fool. ormah (H6195) is a 'gray' word — the serpent's craftiness in Gen 3 — here put to good use: Wisdom does not call the simple to mere innocence but to a shrewdness that can no longer be fooled.

6.text: Listen, for I will speak of noble things, and the opening of my lips will be what is right.
6.amp: Hear [shama — listen, heed], for I will speak [dabar — declare] excellent things [the princely, weighty matters]; the opening of my lips shall be uprightness [meyshar — what is level and straight].
6.notes: shama (H8085) is hearing that obeys, not idle listening. meyshar (H4339) is straightness — speech with no crook or slant in it; Wisdom's words are noble in worth and level in truth, the very opposite of the flatterer's smooth distortions.

7.text: For my mouth utters truth, and wickedness is a thing my lips detest.
7.amp: For my mouth [chek — palate, the inner mouth that tastes] shall meditate [hagah — murmur, give voice to] truth [emeth — faithfulness, reliability]; wickedness [resha] is an abomination [toebah — a detested thing] to my lips.
7.notes: emeth (H571) is truth as utter trustworthiness, the truth one can lean a life on. hagah (H1897) is to mutter or muse aloud, as if truth is what Wisdom's mouth naturally rehearses; resha (H7562) — wickedness — is to her lips a toebah (H8441), the strongest word for moral revulsion.

8.text: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.
8.amp: All the words [emer] of my mouth [peh] are in righteousness [tsedek]; there is nothing twisted [pathal — wreathed, tortuous] or perverse [iqqesh — bent out of true] in them.
8.notes: tsedek (H6664) is righteousness, rightness through and through. pathal (H6617) means wreathed or wrestled into knots, and iqqesh (H6141) means bent off the straight line — the two great defects of crooked speech, both absent from Wisdom's words.

9.text: They are all plain to the one who understands, and right to those who have found knowledge.
9.amp: They are all plain [nakoach — straight, clear, in front of you] to him who understands [biyn], and right [yashar — upright, level] to those who find [matsa] knowledge [daat].
9.notes: nakoach (H5228) is what stands straight in plain view — nothing hidden. Wisdom's words are clear to those willing to learn; the obscurity is never in her speech but in the spurner's heart. To the one who finds daat (H1847), they ring true at once.

10.text: Take my instruction in place of silver, and knowledge rather than the finest gold.
10.amp: Receive [laqach — take, accept] my instruction [musar — corrective discipline], and not silver [keseph]; and knowledge [daat] rather than choice [bachar — select, preferred] gold.
10.notes: musar (H4148) is formative correction, the discipline that shapes a son — the same word as the prologue's second pillar (1:2). Wisdom asks for a deliberate exchange: take her costly correction over precious metal, since what she gives outlasts and outweighs every fortune.

11.text: For wisdom is better than rubies, and nothing you could desire can compare with her.
11.amp: For wisdom [chokmah] is better [tov — good, more excellent] than rubies [precious stones]; all the things one may desire [chephets — delight, what the heart longs for] cannot be compared [shavah — be made equal] to her.
11.notes: shavah (H7737) is to set on the same level; nothing the heart desires (chephets, H2656) can be weighed in the same scale as chokmah. The verse echoes 3:15 and crowns the opening appeal: Wisdom is the one treasure that no other treasure can match.

12.text: I, Wisdom, make my home with prudence, and I find out knowledge and discretion.
12.amp: I, wisdom [chokmah], dwell [shakan — settle, tabernacle] with prudence [ormah — shrewd good sense], and find out [matsa] knowledge [daat] of discretion [mezimmah — the planning, foreseeing mind].
12.notes: shakan (H7931) is settled, abiding dwelling — the root behind the tabernacle. Wisdom and ormah (H6195) live as housemates: true wisdom is never naive but sharp. mezimmah (H4209), the scheming mind that elsewhere serves evil, here becomes foresight ruled by wisdom.

13.text: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil. Pride and arrogance, the evil way, and the mouth that twists the truth — these I hate.
13.amp: The fear [yirah — reverent awe] of the LORD [YHWH] is to hate [sane] evil [ra]; pride [geah], arrogance [gaon — swelling self-exaltation], the evil [ra] way [derek], and the perverse [tahpukot] mouth [peh], I hate [sane].
13.notes: the fear of the LORD (yirah, H3374; YHWH, H3068) is not mere feeling but a settled hatred of evil that mirrors God's own. Pride heads the list — geah (H1344) and gaon (H1347), the self-swelling that the fear of God most directly opposes; cf. 6:16-19.

14.text: Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am understanding, and strength is mine.
14.amp: Counsel [etsah — wise advice, design] is mine, and sound wisdom [tushiyyah — competent wisdom that works, that lasts]; I am understanding [binah — discernment]; I have strength [geburah — might, power].
14.notes: tushiyyah (H8454) is effective, success-bringing wisdom — wisdom that actually holds up under the weight of real life. Counsel and might together (etsah, H6098; geburah, H1369) are royal gifts; the same pairing is prophesied of the Messiah in Isa 11:2, 9:6.

15.text: By me kings reign, and by me rulers decree what is just.
15.amp: By me kings reign [malak — rule as king], and princes decree [chaqaq — engrave, legislate] justice [tsedek — righteousness].
15.notes: chaqaq (H2710) is to inscribe a law as on stone, the act of lawful decree. All rightful authority is borrowed from Wisdom: even the highest thrones rule justly only insofar as they govern by her. Cf. Rom 13:1; Dan 2:21.

16.text: By me princes govern, and nobles — all who rule the earth with justice.
16.amp: By me princes [sar — official, commander] rule [govern, hold sway], and nobles [nadiv — the noble, the willing-hearted], even all the judges [shaphat — those who govern and decide] of the earth [eretz].
16.notes: shaphat (H8199) covers both judging and governing — in Israel the two were one office. Wisdom is the source of every just government on earth; nadiv (H5081) names the noble whose generosity flows from a willing heart, not merely high birth.

17.text: I love those who love me, and those who seek me earnestly will find me.
17.amp: I love [ahab — love, delight in] those who love [ahab] me; and those who seek me early [shachar — seek diligently, at dawn] shall find [matsa] me.
17.notes: ahab (H157) is repeated to bind the love mutual: Wisdom answers love with love. shachar (H7836) means to seek at daybreak, with urgent diligence — to seek wisdom first and eagerly, not as a last resort. The promise echoes Jer 29:13 and Matt 7:7.

18.text: Riches and honor are with me, lasting wealth and righteousness.
18.amp: Riches and honor [kabod — weight, glory] are with me; enduring [durable, abiding] wealth [hon — substance] and righteousness [tsedaqah — right standing and right deeds].
18.notes: kabod (H3519) is honor with weight and substance, not empty show. Wisdom's wealth is paired with tsedaqah (H6666), righteousness — her riches do not corrupt but come bound to integrity, the prosperity that does not rot (cf. v.10; Matt 6:20).

19.text: My fruit is better than gold, even the purest gold, and what I yield surpasses choice silver.
19.amp: My fruit [the harvest I bear] is better [tov] than gold, yes, than fine gold; and my revenue [my yield, my produce] than choice [bachar — selected, preferred] silver [keseph].
19.notes: Wisdom returns to the gold-and-silver comparison of v.10-11, now in terms of fruit and revenue: she is not only a possession but a producing tree, yielding a return that the finest metals cannot rival. Her gain compounds where treasure merely sits.

20.text: I walk in the way of righteousness, along the paths of justice,
20.amp: I lead [halak — walk, go] in the way [orach — path, track] of righteousness [tsedaqah], in the midst [tavek] of the paths [netivah] of justice [mishpat],
20.notes: halak (H1980) means Wisdom herself walks this road — she does not merely point the way but goes ahead in it. tsedaqah (H6666) and mishpat (H4941), righteousness and justice, are the twin tracks she travels; to follow her is to walk where she already walks.

21.text: endowing those who love me with substance, and filling their treasuries full.
21.amp: that I may cause those who love [ahab] me to inherit [nachal — take as lasting possession] substance [yesh — real, abiding being — 'that which is'], and I will fill [male] their treasuries [otsar — storehouse, treasury].
21.notes: nachal (H5157) is to inherit, to receive a permanent possession. yesh (H3426) is striking — literally 'that-which-is,' substance with real being, as opposed to the empty nothings the world chases. Wisdom's reward is the only wealth that truly exists and truly endures.

22.text: The LORD brought me forth at the very beginning of His way, before His works of old.
22.amp: The LORD [YHWH] possessed [qanah — acquired, brought forth, begot] me in the beginning [reshith — the first, the head] of His way [derek], before [qedem — of old, aforetime] His works of old.
22.notes: qanah (H7069) carries both 'possess/acquire' and 'bring forth/beget,' and the ancient debate over Wisdom's origin turns on this word. reshith (H7225) is the same 'beginning' as Gen 1:1. The church reads this not of a created Wisdom but of the eternal Word, begotten of the Father before all worlds (John 1:1-3; Col 1:15-17).

23.text: From eternity I was established, from the very first, before the earth began.
23.amp: I was set up [nasak — poured out, cast, woven] from everlasting [olam — eternity, the boundless past], from the beginning [rosh — the head, the first], before the earth [eretz] was.
23.notes: nasak (H5258) can mean to pour out (as cast metal) or to weave — Wisdom was 'fashioned' or 'installed' from olam (H5769), the immeasurable past. The piling up of time-words — everlasting, beginning, before the earth — presses Wisdom's existence back behind creation itself.

24.text: When there were no ocean depths, I was brought forth, when there were no springs heavy with water.
24.amp: When there were no depths [tehom — the deep, the primeval ocean abyss], I was brought forth [chul — born, brought to birth as in travail]; when there were no fountains [springs] abounding [kabad — heavy, laden] with water.
24.notes: chul (H2342) is the verb of birth-pangs — Wisdom is 'brought forth,' begotten, not assembled. tehom (H8415) is the same primordial deep of Gen 1:2. Before water, before any depth existed, Wisdom already was — a birth that precedes the world's first morning.

25.text: Before the mountains were sunk into place, before the hills, I was brought forth,
25.amp: Before the mountains [har] were settled [sunk, anchored into place], before [panim — the face, the front] the hills [givah], I was brought forth [chul — born, brought to birth];
25.notes: chul (H2342) repeats from v.24, hammering the point: Wisdom was begotten before the oldest, most permanent features of the earth. The mountains, ancient and immovable to human eyes, are themselves younger than she is.

26.text: while as yet He had not made the earth or its open fields, or the first dust of the world.
26.amp: while as yet He had not made [asah — done, fashioned] the earth [eretz], nor the fields [the open lands], nor the highest part [rosh — the head, the sum] of the dust [afar — soil, dry earth] of the world [tebel — the inhabited world].
26.notes: asah (H6213) is to make or fashion. afar (H6083), dust, is the stuff from which man was formed (Gen 2:7); tebel (H8398) is the world as a place for dwellers. Wisdom predates not only the planet but its very first particle of soil.

27.text: When He set the heavens in place, I was there, when He drew the horizon's circle on the face of the deep,
27.amp: When He prepared [kun — established, set firm] the heavens [shamayim], I was there; when He set [chaqaq — inscribed, marked out] a circle [the compass, the horizon's arc] upon the face [panim] of the deep [tehom],
27.notes: kun (H3559) is to establish on a firm footing; chaqaq (H2710), to inscribe, pictures God scribing the great circle of the horizon across the deep. 'I was there' is Wisdom's eyewitness claim: she stood present at the framing of the heavens, not a spectator from outside but a participant within.

28.text: when He fixed the clouds above and the fountains of the deep gushed strong,
28.amp: when He established [amats — made firm, strong] the clouds above; when He strengthened [azaz — made mighty, prevailed] the fountains [ayin — springs, eyes] of the deep [tehom],
28.notes: amats (H553) and azaz (H5810) are both strength-verbs — the clouds set firm above, the deep-springs made to surge with power. ayin (H5869) means both 'eye' and 'spring,' a play picturing the deep's fountains as its watching eyes. Wisdom watched the LORD make even the sky's water and the abyss's force secure.

29.text: when He set the sea its boundary so the waters would not overstep His command, when He marked out the foundations of the earth —
29.amp: when He gave [sum — placed, appointed] to the sea [yam] its decree [choq — statute, fixed limit], that the waters should not pass [abar — cross over] His commandment [peh — mouth, spoken word]; when He appointed [chaqaq — inscribed, decreed] the foundations of the earth [eretz];
29.notes: choq (H2706) is a fixed, engraved statute — the sea's shoreline is law, the boundary God's spoken peh (H6310, 'mouth') will not let it cross (cf. Job 38:8-11; Jer 5:22). chaqaq (H2710) returns from v.27: the same engraving hand that scribed the horizon now decrees the earth's footings.

30.text: then I was beside Him as a master craftsman, and I was His daily delight, rejoicing always before Him,
30.amp: then I was by Him [etsel — at His side, close beside] as a master craftsman [amon — skilled artificer; also nursling, ward]; I was daily His delight [shaashua — joy, sheer delight], rejoicing [sachaq — laughing, playing, exulting] always before [panim — the face of] Him,
30.notes: amon (H525) is gloriously ambiguous — 'master workman' (so the artisan beside the Maker) or 'nursling/little child' (so the cherished one at His side); the church has prized both. sachaq (H7832) is to laugh and play; Wisdom is no grim functionary but the LORD's delight, sporting joyfully in His presence — a glimpse into the gladness within the Godhead before the world was.

31.text: rejoicing in His inhabited world, and my delight was in the sons of men.
31.amp: Rejoicing [sachaq — laughing, playing] in the habitable part [tebel — the inhabited world] of His earth [eretz]; and my delights [shaashua — joys] were with the sons [ben] of men [adam — mankind].
31.notes: sachaq (H7832) and shaashua (H8191) carry over from v.30: the same joy that played before God now overflows toward the inhabited world. The astonishing turn is the last line — Wisdom's delight settles on the bene adam (H1121 + H120), the children of men. The joy of heaven leans earthward, toward us; cf. John 1:14.

32.text: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
32.amp: Now therefore listen [shama — hear and heed] to me, O children [ben — sons]; for blessed [osher — happy, the deep good of the blessed life] are they who keep [shamar — guard, observe] my ways [derek].
32.notes: the sermon turns from cosmic origin to urgent appeal. shamar (H8104) is the watchful keeping that guards a treasure; osher (H835) is the full-orbed blessedness, the same word that opens the Psalter (Ps 1:1). To keep Wisdom's ways is the truly happy life.

33.text: Hear instruction and be wise, and do not turn it away.
33.amp: Hear [shama] instruction [musar — corrective discipline], and be wise [chakam — act wisely], and do not refuse [para — let loose, neglect, fling off] it.
33.notes: musar (H4148) returns from v.10 — corrective discipline is the path to wisdom, not its enemy. para (H6544) means to let loose or cast off, the same verb of refusal as in 1:25; the only fatal error is to wave wisdom away when it is held out to you.

34.text: How happy the man who gives me his ear, keeping watch at my gates day after day, lingering there beside my doorposts!
34.amp: Blessed [osher — happy] is the man [adam] who hears [shama] me, watching [keeping vigil] daily at my gates [doors], waiting [shamar — watching, keeping guard] at the posts of my doorways [petach — entrance].
34.notes: the eager disciple is pictured as a lover at the beloved's door, keeping daily vigil. shamar (H8104) echoes v.32: the one who guards Wisdom's ways is found waiting at her threshold each morning. Such persistent, hungry attention is itself the mark of blessedness.

35.text: Whoever lays hold of me has laid hold of life itself, and from the LORD he draws out His favor.
35.amp: For whoever finds [matsa] me finds life [chay — life itself, living]; and shall obtain [draw out, bring forth] favor [ratzon — delight, acceptance, good pleasure] of the LORD [YHWH].
35.notes: matsa (H4672), to find, has run through the chapter (vv.9, 12, 17) and now reaches its climax: to find Wisdom is to find chay (H2416), life. ratzon (H7522) is the LORD's gracious good pleasure, His accepting delight — the very thing every soul most needs and cannot earn (cf. 3:18; John 14:6).

36.text: But the one who misses me wounds his own soul; all who hate me are in love with death.
36.amp: But he who sins against [chata — misses the mark, fails of] me wrongs [does violence to] his own soul [nephesh]; all who hate [sane] me love [ahab] death [mavet].
36.notes: chata (H2398) literally means to miss the mark — to sin against Wisdom is to fail of the very aim of life, and the self is the victim. The chapter's final, stark either/or: love-words and hate-words collide — to hate Wisdom (sane, H8130) is, whether one knows it or not, to ahab (H157), to love, death itself. The two voices of the whole book end here, in life or in death.
